question.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $100{x}_{2}$, where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}25 \\ -3 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the vector $\mathbf{x}$ below, find the value of $x_2,$ the second component of $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}.$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/d0f25bfafc5ad952775ee1b70be3668322b01ab47415dc2d89a91d4c91f37085.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2,\,\mathbf{q}_3.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/083158484018f1520bd8c8198bd73f17fe37681c3e402d62f8e6d4cd9daa93cb.svg) where $x_i = \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}{\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}.$ 

Computing $x_2,$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-4)}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4+6+8}{1+1+16} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
